title: Safe upgrades: executable, runtime and schema compatibility
goal: Extend the conservative service update boundary with reviewed executable/runtime/schema compatibility before permitting application upgrades
privacy: Neutral fixtures only in git; actual profiles, backups, credentials and deployment evidence remain private.
acceptance: Bind actual input schema and candidate reader/migration behavior to a reviewed source contract and meaningful cross-version regressions before checkout/dependency effects
Preserve source/profile/service ownership, durable fencing, consistent backups, uncertainty and explicit recovery; no marker-only admission or automatic downgrade
Accept real application/runtime upgrade on an explicitly selected target; documentation-only revision changes do not establish this
validation: Directed reader/schema/dependency/update/recovery joins and independent review
Final required CI plus actual target upgrade evidence; never infer migration compatibility from textual markers
escalation: Any destructive restore, changed ownership or unresolved physical/worker effects requires explicit reconciliation; general restore remains F-062

effort.basis: Revised 2026-11-11 after two slices (reader contract and rehearsal merged in PR #257; journaled rehearsal step and refused outcome in review). Remaining: admission beyond documentation, forward recovery, independent review and selected-target acceptance. Migration behavior and review findings remain uncertain; initial estimate was 4–6 focused days.
